docs.title: roBrowser stack documentation
docs.text: The stack has a Node.js/Vite frontend (robrowser) and an independent Apache/PHP RemoteClient (remote). MariaDB, rAthena login/character/map and wsProxy provide the game services. See the repository README for architecture and local client-file layout.

docs.title: Installation versus operation
docs.text:
Situation Procedure New Pi/cluster, no K3s or Longhorn Cluster installation Cluster exists, Ragnarok stack is new Fresh Ragnarok installation Stack already runs under Flux Operations and rollback Local Docker/rAthena or Hercules Deployment and configuration

Do not use infrastructure setup, namespace resets or k8s-all.sh --apply for routine GitOps updates. k8s-all.sh --check is a bootstrap check and rejects active Flux reconcilers; use the read-only checks in the operations guide on an already active cluster.

docs.title: Current validation record
docs.text:
As confirmed by the operator on 2026-11-02: K3s and Longhorn work; flux-system and ragnarok-stack are active/Ready, last confirmed application revision 109430d1; seven Ragnarok pods are Running and ready, and browser login works. PRs #87, #88, #89 and #90 are merged. Historical instructions to keep this namespace deleted or Flux permanently suspended no longer describe operation.

Validation coverage distinguishes executed checks from future installation examples. Graphical/Lua/GRF-content issues remain separate work.

docs.title: Reference
docs.text:
• GitOps lifecycle and release approval
  • Image tags, digests and source revisions
  • Upstream updates
  • Security and private configuration
  • Development and offline tests
  • Vite iframe regression

docs.title: Fresh K3s, Longhorn and Flux cluster
docs.text: This procedure is for a new cluster, not the running Pi. For an existing cluster use the fresh stack runbook or normal operations. The final documentation cleanup executes none of the installation/bootstrap commands below.

docs.title: Infrastructure source and prerequisites
docs.text:
The infrastructure scripts are in the separate custom-scripts repository, under sh/setup-k8s.sh and sh/setup-k8s-flux.sh. Their local source was inspected at commit 7220a191bd06b0ece8b5e42a1f3a04f56751d838; it was not changed. Reinspect later versions rather than assuming this description remains exact.

Prepare the Pi OS/network, a deliberately selected storage device, console/admin access, and a kubeconfig/context identifying the intended cluster. Preserve any existing data. The application additionally needs Git, kubectl, Python 3, bash, envsubst, tar and local client resources; local development/tests need Docker.

docs.title: K3s and Longhorn: setup-k8s.sh
docs.text:
The inspected script:

  • Adds Pi memory-cgroup boot parameters when missing; a reboot may be required.
  • Defaults ROLE=server, INSTALL_LONGHORN=true, MOUNTPOINT=/mnt/longhorn and REPLICA_COUNT=1. K3S_URL/K3S_TOKEN are required for an agent/join operation.
  • Installs iSCSI/NFS/storage prerequisites. If STORAGE_DEVICE is unset, it can auto-detect a non-root disk. After an explicit formatting prompt it can repartition/format it, change fstab and configure Longhorn/bind mounts. Declining formatting still uses/configures the existing partition and mounts.
  • Installs K3s via the upstream installer (no fixed K3s version in this script), copies the server kubeconfig to the real user's ~/.kube/config with mode 0600, and may persist KUBECONFIG in .bashrc. The installer invocation uses K3S_KUBECONFIG_MODE=644 for the system file; protect kubeconfig access accordingly.
  • Installs Helm when needed and installs/upgrades the Longhorn chart at 1.12.1 with defaultReplicaCount and /var/lib/longhorn data path. It marks local-path non-default; verify the actual Longhorn StorageClass/default/replica settings. A chart default does not necessarily rewrite an existing StorageClass.

Example interface, only after explicit new-cluster/storage approval:

# Run from the separately reviewed custom-scripts checkout.
bash sh/setup-k8s.sh

Do not run this to repair a healthy cluster, PVC or application. Check the device and prompt yourself; do not automate a yes response. No new infrastructure installation was re-executed as part of the final documentation verification.

docs.title: Verify the intended context and storage
docs.text:
On the Pi, the setup script normally provides ~/.kube/config. Application scripts otherwise default to the K3s system path; explicitly select the correct file:

export KUBECONFIG="$HOME/.kube/config"
kubectl config current-context
kubectl cluster-info
kubectl get nodes -o wide
kubectl get storageclass
kubectl -n longhorn-system get pods

For remote administration use an authorized kubeconfig with the correct reachable server address, not an unreviewed copy pointing at localhost. Do not print tokens or kubeconfig contents into logs/chat.

docs.title: Flux bootstrap: setup-k8s-flux.sh
docs.text:
The inspected wrapper checks API access, obtains GITHUB_TOKEN by a hidden prompt if absent, installs the Flux CLI if missing, runs flux check --pre, then calls flux bootstrap github with:

  • owner GITHUB_USER (default raiken-mf), repository positional argument/default robrowser_docker;
  • GITHUB_BRANCH (default main) and CLUSTER_PATH (default clusters/pi-cluster);
  • the extra image-reflector/image-automation controllers and --personal;
  • KUBECONFIG from the caller, otherwise ~/.kube/config with a system-file fallback.

It writes bootstrap resources/commits and starts reconciliation. It does not create application Secrets from .env, populate client data, install the MariaDB operator, or automatically suspend either Kustomization.

docs.title: Gate a genuinely fresh cluster before application reconciliation
docs.text:
Current main describes an active ragnarok-stack (suspend:false). Bootstrapping it onto an empty cluster can start the stack before private prerequisites exist. Do not use the normal active main as though it were a paused installation plan.

For a new cluster, first prepare an operator-reviewed installation branch with the same clusters/pi-cluster path and an explicit ragnarok-stack suspend:true. Keep the running cluster on its existing main; do not merge a global pause as part of documentation maintenance. Bootstrap that reviewed branch, for example:

# Interface example: INSTALL_BRANCH must already exist and hold the child paused.
: "${INSTALL_BRANCH:?Set the existing reviewed installation branch first}"
GITHUB_BRANCH="$INSTALL_BRANCH" CLUSTER_PATH=clusters/pi-cluster \
  bash sh/setup-k8s-flux.sh robrowser_docker

This branch-based fresh-cluster gate is derived from the inspected interfaces; it was not re-executed/claimed as a new verified install during this cleanup. Never use a nonexistent placeholder branch. Verify the child is suspended before pausing the parent for manual application bootstrap. Any suspend/resume commands are installation actions requiring their own approval, not normal health checks.

docs.title: Complete prerequisites before the application
docs.text:
Longhorn alone is insufficient. The application requires a ready MariaDB operator, webhook and k8s.mariadb.com CRDs; K3s/Longhorn setup does not supply them. The existing k8s-mariadb.sh can install/upgrade that operator but ALSO creates application resources/secrets, so it is not a harmless check. Have the operator provision the required infrastructure in an approved stage. On the verified Pi it was already installed and available before k8s-all.sh.

Continue with fresh Ragnarok installation, keeping both application reconcilers paused until their controlled activation. Future moves from a staging branch to main must be reviewed in both the GitRepository spec and bootstrap files; do not repeat bootstrap against the running cluster.

docs.title: Architecture
docs.text:
Image / service Contents Build tree robrowser Node.js, Vite, pinned roBrowserLegacy frontend images/robrowser remote Apache, PHP 8.4, PHP RemoteClient, ROEnglishRE, client resources images/remote wsproxy WebSocket proxy to internal game services images/wsproxy rathena Login/character/map servers images/rathena hercules Alternative Compose game-server image images/hercules

The Apache image does not clone or contain the frontend. Only the frontend owns index.html.template. /remote/ and the pinned RemoteClient .htaccess remain on the Apache service; / on that service is its static status page.

docs.title: Configuration sources
docs.text:
.env-tmpl is a starting template; preserve/edit the existing local .env. Never commit passwords, private bootstrap output or client assets.

Setting Template/Pi value Compose fallback Kubernetes fallback Internal port PORT_FRONTEND 30000 3000 30000 3000 PORT_HTTP 30080 8080 30080 8080 PORT_WSPROXY 30599 5999 30599 5999

Compose uses these variables for host ports; Kubernetes templates use them for NodePorts. Changing them does not change container listeners/target ports. HOST must resolve from the browser: the verified Pi configuration uses HOST=pi. Internal names database and ragnarok-login are not public browser hostnames; wsProxy resolves game-service names inside the cluster/network.

  • Compose: the root .env supplies interpolation and explicit service env_file configuration; mounts refer to this checkout's client/ directories.
  • Full bootstrap: k8s-all.sh honors ENV_FILE (default repository .env), CLIENT_SOURCE_DIR (default repository client), K8S_NAMESPACE (default ragnarok) and KUBECONFIG (default /etc/rancher/k3s/k3s.yaml). It changes to the repository root internally. Use absolute ENV_FILE/CLIENT_SOURCE_DIR paths when running from another worktree.
  • Offline renderers: render-web-manifests.sh honors ENV_FILE; render-k8s-bootstrap.py accepts --env-file explicitly.
  • Flux: reads deploy/k8s/ through deploy/overlays/flux; it does not read local .env, rerun the renderer or upload local client files.
  • Legacy component scripts: several still source .env directly. They are not the normal GitOps update path and do not all implement ENV_FILE semantics.

The web ConfigMap contains HOST, the three ports, SERVER_NAME, SET_PRERENEWAL and PACKETVER. rathena-config contains non-secret DB/game configuration. The private bootstrap Secret supplies both password (operator) and MARIADB_PASSWORD (game containers), plus configured interserver credentials. Passwords never belong in a Git-managed ConfigMap.

docs.title: Image-tag compatibility
docs.text:
VITE_IMAGE_TAG still selects the frontend/robrowser image. Legacy ROBROWSER_IMAGE_TAG remains an Apache/remote fallback; REMOTE_IMAGE_TAG takes precedence for that service. RATHENA_IMAGE_TAG and WSPROXY_IMAGE_TAG remain. Do not silently reinterpret these existing variables during the image rename.

k8s-all.sh defaults to reviewed SHA tags from the Flux overlay and rejects empty or stable selections. The standalone renderer/component scripts can default to stable, so explicitly select reviewed releases before using their output for production. See Image revisions.

docs.title: Docker Compose
docs.text:
Docker Engine/Compose and local client files are prerequisites. From repository root, validate without printing the expanded environment:

docker compose --env-file .env -f deploy/compose/docker-compose-common.yml -f deploy/compose/docker-compose-rathena.yml config --quiet

Starting Compose changes local containers; use it only for the intended local installation, not to update a Kubernetes deployment:

./start.sh rathena detached
./start.sh hercules detached

The first argument selects the emulator; ./start.sh detached is not valid. Default ./start.sh runs rAthena in the foreground. ./start.sh stop stops the Compose stacks. These are script interfaces, not commands executed during the final documentation cleanup.

docs.title: Kubernetes
docs.text:
Cluster setup, fresh stack installation and normal operation are separate procedures. Existing K3s, Longhorn, MariaDB operator and Flux must not be reinstalled as routine updates.

To review web manifests without changing the cluster:

ENV_FILE=/absolute/path/to/.env bash scripts/render-web-manifests.sh /tmp/ragnarok-web-review
kubectl kustomize deploy/overlays/flux

The renderer emits remote.yaml, robrowser.yaml, wsproxy.yaml and robrowser-config.yaml. Review ports, namespace, public HOST, image references and non-secret values before proposing Git changes. It does not automatically replace the concrete manifests or update Flux. Never copy private bootstrap output into deploy/k8s/.

docs.title: Translation, mounts and overrides
docs.text:
The remote build copies Renewal data and SystemEN (installed as remote/System) from pinned ROEnglishRE. SET_PRERENEWAL=1 is a build argument adding the Pre-Renewal layer afterwards. Runtime changes cannot rebuild those translations. Required source directories are checked; optional Addons/Compatibility layers are not silently installed.

images/remote/repository_override/ is copied after translations into the Apache document root. Use remote/data and remote/System for translation overrides. images/robrowser/repository_override/ is copied into /app after npm install and the default frontend template. Most local payloads stay ignored by Git and are not present in clean CI builds; the two API-module fix files are intentional versioned exceptions. See the iframe fix.

At startup, remote merges readonly /opt/client_files/data and System into its writable translation tree, preserving the base and giving user loose files precedence. Resources/BGM/AI retain their readonly mounts. Bootstrap uploads local assets into the client-data PVC before starting the web deployments.

docs.title: Existing-checkout override folder rename
docs.text: Git does not move ignored user files. If converting an OLD checkout, preserve the old Apache images/robrowser/repository_override payload under images/remote, and the old images/vite/repository_override frontend payload under images/robrowser. Do not mix the two runtime payloads. This is a manual local-file migration, not a reason to reset a namespace or overwrite working assets.

docs.title: Ownership
docs.text:
• images/robrowser: Node.js/Vite frontend, package/lockfile overlay and client template.
  • images/remote: Apache/PHP, RemoteClient, translations and client-file configuration.
  • images/rathena and images/hercules: game-server images; images/wsproxy: proxy.
  • build/dependencies.env: exact upstream Git revision pins.
  • deploy/compose: local runtime; deploy/k8s: concrete GitOps base; deploy/k8s-templates: .env-based bootstrap/preview templates; deploy/overlays/flux: reviewed release selection.
  • clusters/pi-cluster: Flux parent/source and child application configuration.
  • scripts: bootstrap, renderers and isolated validation helpers.
  • docs: installation, operation, development, release and security guidance.

The separate custom-scripts repository owns K3s/Longhorn/Flux bootstrap wrappers; it is not vendored here. Do not change its storage/bootstrap behavior as a side effect of an application or documentation fix.

docs.title: Safe local work
docs.text:
Use a feature branch or separate worktree based on current main. Keep existing .env, client assets and ignored overrides outside any cleanup/reset operation. Never run broad git clean, hard resets or image/volume pruning to make a checkout look tidy. Inspect the worktree's tracked, untracked AND ignored files before removing it; archive any configuration that must survive.

A branch is not proved merged merely because its PR is closed: rebased/squashed history may need further review. Preserve ambiguous refs rather than force-delete them. Remote-branch deletion requires explicit permission.

The full bootstrap can use absolute ENV_FILE and CLIENT_SOURCE_DIR paths from another worktree. Compose's bind paths/env_file remain rooted in its checkout; ENV_FILE is not a general Compose override. See deployment.

docs.title: Build the two web images
docs.text:
These commands build local test images, not Kubernetes deployments or registry releases. Source the versioned dependency pins, not an arbitrary upstream HEAD:

set -a
source build/dependencies.env
set +a
docker build -f images/remote/Dockerfile \
  --build-arg REMOTECLIENT_REPOSITORY="$REMOTECLIENT_REPOSITORY" \
  --build-arg REMOTECLIENT_REF="$REMOTECLIENT_REF" \
  --build-arg ROENGLISH_REPOSITORY="$ROENGLISH_REPOSITORY" \
  --build-arg ROENGLISH_REF="$ROENGLISH_REF" -t remote:ci .
docker build -f images/robrowser/Dockerfile \
  --build-arg ROBROWSER_REPOSITORY="$ROBROWSER_REPOSITORY" \
  --build-arg ROBROWSER_REF="$ROBROWSER_REF" -t robrowser:ci .

The remote build accepts SET_PRERENEWAL=1 for its additional translation layer. The frontend alone fetches roBrowserLegacy; do not add that source tree to remote. Project-owned npm manifest/lockfile are installed with npm ci. Update the lockfile and source pin together when the new upstream revision needs a dependency change.

docs.title: Validation without Kubernetes deployment
docs.text:
Offline/fake-API checks:

python3 scripts/check-k8s-bootstrap.py
python3 scripts/check-k8s-all.py
kubectl kustomize deploy/overlays/flux >/dev/null

The bootstrap tests use synthetic fixtures/fake kubectl, check confidentiality, abort paths and component ordering. They do not install a real stack. Real k8s-all.sh --check contacts the selected cluster read-only and expects paused Flux; it is unsuitable as an active-cluster CI/operations command.

After building the local images, the Docker checks start/remove their own test containers/networks. Do not confuse them with cluster acceptance:

bash scripts/check-roenglish.sh remote:ci
bash scripts/check-image-boundaries.sh remote:ci robrowser:ci
python3 scripts/check-image-overrides.py
python3 scripts/check-api-module.py robrowser:ci
python3 scripts/check-compose.py remote:ci robrowser:ci

check-compose.py reads this checkout's .env and actual Compose configuration, then isolates the web services on temporary networks and loopback ephemeral ports. CLIENT_TEST_ROOT optionally points to readonly client fixtures. check-roenglish.sh builds/tests the additional Pre-Renewal variant. The upstream-layout check clones pinned sources temporarily; it does not modify their original repositories.

The API iframe override is bound to the pinned upstream HTML. The layout gate detects changes needing a rebase. Other local override payloads stay ignored and are not supplied to clean GitHub Actions builds.

docs.title: CI build caches and release boundaries
docs.text:
The required validate job runs on every pull request, including documentation changes; documentation-only PRs skip Docker builds. Relevant changes exercise all web and proxy smoke tests because they validate cross-service integration. rAthena validation builds only when its inputs or dependency pins change. Hercules is Compose-config validated but is not built or published by CI.

Buildx stores AMD64 test layers in separate GitHub Actions scopes ci-remote-amd64, ci-robrowser-amd64, ci-wsproxy-amd64 and ci-rathena-amd64. Renewal and Pre-Renewal remote builds share the same local Buildx builder in the validation job, as do the isolated override fixtures. GitHub isolates PR caches from main; never store credentials in layers or cache. BuildKit matches Dockerfile commands, base images, build arguments and copied inputs, so affected layers and subsequent layers rebuild when their inputs change. External package repositories are not cache keys: cached test images are not proof that the latest patches were fetched.

Release candidates are built separately on main and scanned on both AMD64 and ARM64. The remote and robrowser release builds deliberately use no-cache to refresh mutable OS packages. wsproxy retains its uncached release build. rAthena imports the AMD64 CI scope and its multi-platform GHCR buildcache and exports only the latter; BuildKit matches platform-specific layers. The scoped CI cache has one writer per workflow/ref, while the release cache has one writer per image and main CI runs are serialized. Publish promotes the exact security-approved candidate digests; it never rebuilds from these caches. The scans, SBOMs, release tags and draft image-pin PR remain mandatory and unchanged.

On a cold or evicted cache, BuildKit rebuilds normally; exports use ignore-error=true so an unavailable cache does not skip a test. Inspect the build action's import/export messages and CACHED lines, image scope, branch, platform and changed build arguments when diagnosing misses. GitHub cache eviction, limits and first-run warmup affect hit rates. To diagnose stale cache, compare a fresh no-cache test build and inspect its inputs; do not bypass release scans. BuildKit cache mounts are not exported by the GHA backend by default, so no cross-run npm cache-mount persistence is assumed.

docs.title: Documentation checks
docs.text:
The existing documentation workflow installs mkdocs-material and publishes the site on main changes to docs or mkdocs.yml. A local strict build is the relevant pre-PR check:

python3 -m venv /tmp/robrowser-docs-tools
/tmp/robrowser-docs-tools/bin/pip install mkdocs-material
/tmp/robrowser-docs-tools/bin/mkdocs build --strict --site-dir /tmp/robrowser-docs-site

Use a fresh temporary directory if those paths already contain someone else's work. Do not commit generated site files, test output, reports or private bootstrap artifacts. PR CI's required validate check is scope-sensitive: documentation-only changes do not exercise image builds. Record the actual local/CI checks in the PR.

docs.title: Contribution scope
docs.text: Keep changes small, describe behavior and validation, and obtain the appropriate merge/deployment approvals. Current application fixes use their own reviewed PRs; remaining graphics/Lua/GRF-content/gameplay issues are outside documentation cleanup. See validation boundaries and security.

docs.title: Fresh Ragnarok stack on an existing cluster
docs.text: This runbook is for an empty application installation on an already prepared cluster. It is not the maintenance procedure for the running GitOps stack. The Pi installation has completed: both Flux Kustomizations are active/Ready and browser login succeeded. Nothing here says to suspend that working installation.

docs.title: Prerequisites and approval gate
docs.text:
K3s/node access, Longhorn, a ready MariaDB operator/webhook and its CRDs must already exist. The cluster guide explains the separate infrastructure scripts and their side effects. k8s-all.sh checks these prerequisites; it does not install/upgrade them.

For a genuinely new stack, obtain installation approval, review storage and image pins, and ensure the target namespace is absent. Do not delete a working namespace or reuse this procedure as a backup restore. The verified installation deliberately used a new empty ragnarok database; no old data required recovery.

The manual bootstrap requires both existing Flux Kustomizations paused. The Git state used for activation must hold ragnarok-stack at suspend:true until its release is approved. See controlled activation. The current operational main has suspend:false; it is not an installation hold. Establish a reviewed hold for the target installation before bootstrap, rather than assuming a one-off pause survives parent reconciliation.

docs.title: Local configuration and context
docs.text:
Use a reviewed current checkout without overwriting local .env, client files or ignored override payloads. A separate worktree can use the originals by absolute path. For example, after choosing the intended checkout:

export KUBECONFIG=/etc/rancher/k3s/k3s.yaml
export ENV_FILE=/home/pi/git/robrowser_docker/.env
export CLIENT_SOURCE_DIR=/home/pi/git/robrowser_docker/client
kubectl config current-context
kubectl get nodes -o wide
flux get kustomizations -n flux-system

These are environment/read-only checks. Never print kubeconfig, .env, Secret data or registry credentials. On another host use its authorized kubeconfig; copying a Pi file with a localhost server address is not sufficient.

The verified Pi uses HOST=pi, PORT_FRONTEND=30000, PORT_HTTP=30080 and PORT_WSPROXY=30599. Keep the existing variable names and fallbacks. All database and interserver credentials are read from local .env exactly as configured; bootstrap does not invent passwords or restore backups.

Expected local layout:

client/
  resources/DATA.INI   # case-sensitive, references the available GRFs
  resources/*.grf
  AI/
  BGM/
  data/
  System/

Before installation, verify source files fit the 15Gi client PVC. MariaDB uses new 5Gi Longhorn storage. A previous namespace's Bound PVC status does not establish a recovery path after deletion; this runbook assumes an empty new DB.

docs.title: Read-only bootstrap check
docs.text:
bash scripts/k8s-all.sh --check

No argument also defaults to --check. It loads the local configuration, renders private temporary Secrets/ConfigMaps, checks API errors, operator/storage availability, image tag selection, paused Flux, port ownership and DATA.INI/GRF source completeness. It performs no cluster writes and removes its private temporary files. It intentionally rejects active Flux even though this mode is read-only; it is a bootstrap preflight, not a general operations health check.

The web renderer can emit non-secret review files separately, but its standalone image defaults may be stable. The full bootstrap chooses reviewed SHA tags from the Flux overlay unless compatible image-tag overrides were explicitly supplied. Review those overrides; never treat an invented old-name SHA or stable as release provenance. See configuration sources.

docs.title: Full installation — changes the cluster
docs.text:
Only after the installation approval and a successful preflight:

bash scripts/k8s-all.sh --apply

The script runs the complete application sequence:

  1. Recheck paused Flux/prerequisites. An existing namespace requires an expressly approved --reconcile retry. API/auth failures abort, not masquerade as NotFound. The script never deletes a namespace or resumes Flux.
  2. Apply the labeled/hardened namespace and restrictive DB network policy, then private mariadb-root-secret/mariadb-user-secret and rathena-config, followed by the .env-derived robrowser-config.
  3. Apply MariaDB, Database, User and Grant CRs and wait for their Ready conditions. The user Secret contains both password (operator) and MARIADB_PASSWORD (rAthena), plus the configured interserver user/password. No password goes in a Git-managed ConfigMap or local command argument.
  4. Create the client PVC/non-root loader, upload CLIENT_SOURCE_DIR folders and check streamed file sizes. Stop on failure before starting the web services.
  5. Start login, char and map in dependency order. Login's INIT_DB=true entrypoint imports the empty schema and Renewal/Pre-Renewal SQL according to SET_PRERENEWAL, then configures the interserver account. Char/map do not initialize the DB. A private in-pod SQL check verifies the account row.
  6. Deploy/wait for wsProxy, remote and robrowser. Check an actual wsProxy WebSocket handshake and parse the mounted first GRF using RemoteClient PHP. List pods/services/PVCs; Flux remains paused for the separate adoption gate.

Secret output is an owner-only temporary file (directory 0700, file 0600), not logged or committed. The offline renderer rejects overwriting an existing output file. A failure aborts; it does not reset data or suppress SQL failures. Diagnose it before approving --apply --reconcile for a partial-install retry.

docs.title: Acceptance and GitOps adoption
docs.text:
Use the read-only operations checks, then test the frontend in a real browser: rendered host/ports, iframe startup, RemoteClient requests/CORS, external WebSocket connection, login and map loading. Keep client content errors distinct from Kubernetes readiness.

For first adoption, activate the parent while the child is explicitly held in Git; verify parent revision/Ready and the child pause, then separately review the Git change enabling the child. See the precise sequence. Git-managed configuration/pins must match the installed .env-derived settings. Secrets and populated client contents remain private/bootstrap managed; do not commit or recreate them to make GitOps adopt the stack.

docs.title: What was actually verified
docs.text: The completed Pi installation and login were confirmed by the operator on 2026-11-02. The empty MariaDB 11.8.6 schema/bootstrap was also tested in disposable Docker containers against the published rAthena image. CI tests secret rendering, failure/ordering behavior through a fake kubectl, and the frontend/remote images. Those fake-API tests are not substitutes for live acceptance. Commands in this runbook are future procedures and were not re-executed during documentation cleanup.

docs.title: Vite iframe HTML-proxy regression
docs.text: The pinned upstream applications/api/api.js creates a FRAME URL as api.html? + Math.random() + location.hash. On a cold Vite server, requesting that cache-busted page transformed the inline module into api.html?html-proxy&index=0.js. That module request returned HTTP 500: No matching HTML proxy module found. Warming the unqueried HTML first can hide the problem, which is why the old root/API-script HTTP smoke checks missed it.

docs.title: Project-owned override
docs.text:
images/robrowser/repository_override/applications/api/api.html changes only the inline module into <script type="module" src="./api-bootstrap.js"></script>. The neighboring api-bootstrap.js contains the exact extracted upstream logic. Its relative dynamic import still resolves to ../../src/main.js because the external module stays in the same directory as the HTML page.

Parent/opener source filtering, the one-shot configuration listener, ROConfig assignment before the import, the ready reply after successful import and the error handler are preserved. The import map, styles/preloader and HTML remain. The random query, Firefox/hash behavior and upstream api.js are unchanged. No upstream repository, package dependency, source revision, runtime security, port setting or Kubernetes resource is changed.

These two files are intentionally versioned exceptions to the local override ignore rules. Other custom override payloads remain ignored. A source-pin update must recheck this extraction: check-upstream-layout.sh runs check-api-override.py against the actual fetched upstream HTML and rejects a stale override instead of silently masking an upstream bootstrap change.

docs.title: Regression checks
docs.text:
After building the normal pinned frontend image:

python3 scripts/check-api-module.py robrowser:ci

The test starts/removes its own container on an ephemeral loopback host port. It first requests query-bearing iframe HTML without warming the unqueried page, fetches every module URL returned by Vite, and verifies JavaScript/HTTP 200 for several query/hash/no-query variants. It also requests the real transformed /src/main.js entry. The same test fails against the pre-fix image with the original HTTP 500 proxy error.

check-api-handshake.cjs then executes the real api.js and the Vite-served external bootstrap using Node VM modules. It checks random iframe URLs, config polling/ready cleanup, rejected foreign-window messages, parent and opener initialization, one-shot setup, delayed import readiness and import failure. Only engine execution is stubbed here: the real engine URL is independently requested through Vite. This is not a full graphical browser/gameplay test. The regression is required in PR/main CI and needs no added npm dependencies.

docs.title: Verification and current deployment
docs.text:
Local ARM64 tests reproduced the old 500 response and passed after extraction. CI includes the HTTP/module and handshake checks. The fix merged in PR #88; its published ARM64-capable frontend release was selected through PR #89. After the completed Kubernetes/GitOps adoption the operator confirmed successful browser login. Both Flux Kustomizations are now active/Ready; the former paused installation state is no longer an operating instruction.

These tests do not close separate graphics, Lua, GRF-content or gameplay issues. See validation coverage and normal operations.

docs.title: Source of truth and current state
docs.text:
clusters/pi-cluster/flux-system/gotk-sync.yaml defines the GitRepository and parent Kustomization flux-system. The parent reconciles clusters/pi-cluster and therefore manages the child object in ragnarok-app.yaml. Both use the same source. The child ragnarok-stack reconciles deploy/overlays/flux, whose base is deploy/k8s. There is no explicit dependsOn in these manifests; the parent/child management relationship is not an application-health dependency.

The verified operating state has both reconcilers active/Ready. The child Git spec is suspend:false. An absent suspend field on the parent also means active. The last operator-confirmed installation revision was 109430d1 (2026-11-02); later documentation-only merges can advance source/applied revisions without changing workload specifications.

Local .env is not read by Flux. Review and commit non-secret ConfigMaps, selectors, ports and release pins explicitly. Private bootstrap supplies Secrets and client PVC contents. wait:false on the application means Flux Ready proves reconciliation, not healthy DB/game/frontend processes.

docs.title: Controlled first activation
docs.text:
This section is for a new installation, not normal operation. It describes the hold used during installation; it is not a request to reapply it to today's working stack.

  1. Have a reviewed Git installation state explicitly holding the child at suspend:true. During manual bootstrap both existing reconcilers stay paused. The full application installer refuses an active reconciler and never resumes it.
  2. After bootstrap/acceptance and activation approval, confirm the intended source revision and SSH Secret. Resume only the parent while the Git child hold remains true; wait for the parent's Ready condition and exact applied revision. Verify the child remains suspended. Do not infer application health from this.
  3. Review a separate Git change lifting the child hold (suspend:false). With the parent active, merging it lets the parent update the child and start its reconciliation. A one-off CLI child resume while Git still says true is not durable: the parent would restore the hold.
  4. Verify both Flux revisions/conditions, then actual pods, PVCs, endpoints, frontend, RemoteClient, WebSocket and browser login. Resolve manifest drift from any .env-based manual bootstrap before accepting GitOps ownership.

The completed installation used the reviewed child activation in PR #90. Do not repeat bootstrap or pause/resume working reconcilers for a routine image update.

docs.title: Normal approved-release path
docs.text:
1. Source/dependency changes pass required PR validation and enter main through review or the repository's configured dependency auto-merge policy.
  2. Main CI validates the affected images. Container Security builds changed candidates for AMD64/ARM64, applies the existing HIGH/CRITICAL vulnerability gate and emits platform SBOMs/approved digest records.
  3. Publish promotes the exact scanned digests, checks their source revision and rejects publication if main moved during the scan. It sets sha-source and stable tags; unchanged components retain their previous releases.
  4. Publish opens a draft GitOps image-bump PR, without enabling auto-merge, updating only the corresponding overlay image tags.
  5. Review the actual registry digest/source/platforms, CI, component pairing and release approval, then merge that image-pin PR. Active Flux automatically applies the new Git desired state; a manual reconcile command is not required.

This is automatic adoption after approval, not automatic approval of all published images. Publishing stable alone does not change SHA-pinned pods. Review any externally configured auto-merge separately; it is not promised by these workflows. See upstream updates for the distinct source-PR and Dependabot auto-merge rules.

docs.title: Normal inspection and optional reconciliation
docs.text:
Read-only:

flux get sources git -n flux-system
flux get kustomizations -n flux-system
kubectl -n flux-system get kustomizations flux-system ragnarok-stack

If an operator explicitly needs to accelerate an approved desired-state change, these are mutating reconciliation requests, not passive health checks:

flux reconcile source git flux-system -n flux-system
flux reconcile kustomization flux-system -n flux-system --with-source
flux reconcile kustomization ragnarok-stack -n flux-system --with-source

Do not run them, resume/suspend Flux or bootstrap the cluster during unrelated documentation/cleanup work. Normal polling already reconciles Git automatically.

docs.title: Recovering from a bad release
docs.text:
Prefer a reviewed Git revert to the last verified component tag/digest, preserving other image pins and configuration. Once merged, verify Flux and application health. Do not substitute newest main into every component tag or roll stable back blindly.

An imperative deployment-only rollback is an emergency action needing explicit approval and coordination with active Flux; otherwise it will reconcile back to Git. Record the previous reference, actual container name and scope. Never use namespace/PVC deletion as rollback, and never restore DB storage without a separate verified recovery plan. See operations.

docs.title: Image references and provenance
docs.text: The authoritative desired selection is deploy/overlays/flux/kustomization.yaml, not whichever local test image or stable tag happens to exist.

docs.title: Verified installation selection
docs.text:
The following source tags were selected at the confirmed 109430d1 operating baseline (2026-11-02). This table is a dated reference; future approved image PRs can update the overlay independently per component.

Image Role Selected source tag robrowser Node.js/Vite frontend, including the iframe module fix sha-d32fa0e2a793eac80274fcc8d1206a871f4a1376 remote Apache/PHP/RemoteClient/ROEnglishRE sha-6c00eb847d9f65c9b0f4c941140b790177c37470 rathena Login/char/map servers sha-a9c11e46784f25a75cd85cb91cc7fe97e41533f9 wsproxy Game WebSocket proxy sha-ddc424509d376dc1e77f4b6925f3df37fc4caf27

The final-name releases support AMD64 and ARM64. The frontend d32fa0e release passed main CI/security/SBOM/promotion in run 41448256973. The initial final-name web release passed run 41435931124. Those are evidence for those releases, not a claim that later unchanged images were rescanned on every documentation/image-pin commit.

docs.title: Source SHA versus registry digest
docs.text:
• build/dependencies.env pins upstream source repositories. Their commit hashes are not infrastructure release tags.
  • sha-infrastructure-commit tags identify the source build revision for each released image. Components can legitimately have different tags when their build inputs did not change.
  • The OCI org.opencontainers.image.revision annotation records the build source.
  • sha256:… is the exact registry manifest/index digest. A SHA-named tag is still a tag; verify its digest/platform/provenance rather than treating its spelling as cryptographic immutability. stable is explicitly mutable.
  • Newest main can be a documentation/manifest-only commit with no image release. Do not substitute main HEAD into all tags or compare SHA strings alphabetically.

With Docker/buildx available, inspect the actual selected registry reference; this does not deploy it:

docker buildx imagetools inspect ghcr.io/raiken-mf/robrowser:sha-d32fa0e2a793eac80274fcc8d1206a871f4a1376

Check the exact digest, source annotation, both architectures and corresponding successful security/promotion artifacts. Runtime inspection should match the intended role: frontend has Node/Vite, remote has Apache/PHP and client files.

docs.title: Adoption and rollback
docs.text:
The generated draft GitOps PR supplies reviewed tags only for changed images. With active Flux, merging the approved pin change deploys it automatically; publishing a registry tag does not update an already SHA-pinned Deployment. Do not infer automatic merge approval from installed Flux image controllers.

Record the prior component reference before a rollout. Roll back to its verified tag/digest through a narrow Git change, retaining the other image pins. Follow operations for explicitly approved emergency imperative changes. No old pre-rename Apache image should be mistaken for today's frontend robrowser image.

docs.title: Client resources with the unmodified PHP RemoteClient
docs.text:
The RemoteClient is pinned to the PHP fork's revert merge; its source tree is identical to the pre-custom-resolver revision. CLIENT_RESPATH and CLIENT_DATAINI select the directory containing DATA.INI and GRFs; the existing resources mount supplies them. Its original PHP fallback accepts data/ and BGM/ requests and searches the local data tree and GRFs. It does not provide SYSTEM_PATH, SYSTEMEN_PATH, AI_PATH, DATA_OVERRIDE_PATH, or a System to SystemEN alias.

The image installs ROEnglishRE's original SystemEN tree once, at its original path. Apache can serve existing static SystemEN/ files directly. The existing roBrowser customItemInfo option selects SystemEN/itemInfo.lua, which loads its original nested SystemEN files. System/ is a separate symlink to the read-only client-data mount, so real original System files remain accessible. Missing SystemEN/, System/ and AI/ files are not resolved from GRFs by the PHP fallback. One Apache redirect maps a missing AI/Util.lua request to the existing data/ai/util.lua GRF path; a loose AI/Util.lua takes priority. The redirect has a relative location and includes the existing CORS policy. The frontend proxies /remote/ to the RemoteClient so browser requests and the redirect remain on the frontend origin in Compose and Kubernetes. An internal rewrite alone cannot replace the redirect: the upstream PHP 404 handler reads the original request URI, so it searches for AI/Util.lua instead of the GRF's data/ai/util.lua. The image also installs ROEnglishRE's PetEvolution.lub once in SystemEN/. Apache serves it for a missing System/PetEvolutionCln.lub; a loose original takes priority. Other System/ requests are not mapped to SystemEN/. Existing AI and BGM mounts are exposed by the image's existing symlinks. The image does not copy external PVC data/ files into its own tree at startup; those files cannot be overlaid together with baked files using a supported PHP setting. No copies or changes to original client files are made. If those overlays or virtual aliases are required, the unmodified software does not provide them and a separate decision is needed.

The pinned client's TownInfo callback returns no success value and replaces each map's entries. The supplied English Towninfo stops after its first callback; serving it at a different path does not fix that client incompatibility. The client already falls back from the missing System quest aliases to SystemEN/OngoingQuests.lub; its Lua 5.1 execution creates 11,363 entries.

The optional System/Font/SCDream4.otf, data/msgstringtable.csv, System/OngoingQuestInfoList.lub, System/Towninfo.lub, AI/AI_M.lua and data/luafiles514/lua files/hateffectinfo/hateffectids.lub depend on the operator's client data. They are not supplied as placeholders. Availability and warnings vary with the mounted loose files and GRFs.

The image retains upstream request handling and applies standard Apache access controls to protect GRFs, configuration, application PHP files and internal directories from direct HTTP access.

docs.title: Existing GitOps cluster: operation and recovery
docs.text: The Pi stack is installed. Both Flux Kustomizations are active/Ready and seven application pods were confirmed Running/ready with successful browser login on 2026-11-02. Do not use setup-k8s.sh, setup-k8s-flux.sh, k8s-all.sh --apply, namespace resets or blanket image/volume pruning for routine maintenance.

docs.title: Health checks
docs.text:
Select the intended authorized kubeconfig/context before any action. On pi the application scripts default to /etc/rancher/k3s/k3s.yaml; an operator can instead explicitly use the user kubeconfig created by infrastructure setup:

export KUBECONFIG="$HOME/.kube/config"
kubectl config current-context
kubectl get nodes -o wide
flux get sources git -n flux-system
flux get kustomizations -n flux-system
kubectl -n ragnarok get deployments,statefulsets,pods
kubectl -n ragnarok get pvc,services,endpointslices
kubectl -n ragnarok get events --field-selector type=Warning --sort-by=.lastTimestamp
kubectl -n longhorn-system get pods
kubectl get storageclass

These commands inspect state; they do not reconcile/install/restart resources. Expected application roles: database-0 (operator StatefulSet), rAthena login/char/map, remote, robrowser and wsProxy. There are six application Deployments plus MariaDB; the confirmed one-replica baseline has seven pods, each 1/1. Names/counts can change with a deliberate reviewed scaling/version change.

Check Ready/available replicas, Bound PVCs, populated EndpointSlices, current Flux source/applied revision and no repeated scheduling/pull/crash errors. Longhorn controller readiness and an existing StorageClass alone do not prove volume health or data recovery; inspect actual relevant volumes when investigating a storage incident, without deleting them.

Read-only workload details, scoped to the actual failing service:

kubectl -n ragnarok describe deployment robrowser
kubectl -n ragnarok logs deployment/robrowser --tail=100
kubectl -n ragnarok logs deployment/remote --tail=100
kubectl -n ragnarok get deployments -o custom-columns=NAME:.metadata.name,IMAGE:.spec.template.spec.containers[*].image

Do not dump Secret data, full environments, kubeconfigs or remote URLs with embedded credentials. Sanitize console/network diagnostics, including tokens in Vite/HMR WebSocket query strings, before sharing reports.

docs.title: HTTP, module and game checks
docs.text:
The verified Pi configuration uses these public URLs; for another installation use its actual HOST/ports, not internal cluster DNS names:

curl -fsS http://pi:30080/ >/dev/null
curl -fsS http://pi:30080/remote/System/add-system-folder-files-here.txt >/dev/null
curl -fsS http://pi:30000/ >/dev/null
curl -fsS http://pi:30000/applications/api/api.js >/dev/null
curl -fsS 'http://pi:30000/applications/api/api.html?0.138571' >/dev/null
curl -fsS http://pi:30000/applications/api/api-bootstrap.js >/dev/null
curl -fsS http://pi:30000/src/Renderer/GR2/GR2ModelRenderer.js >/dev/null

A successful HTML request is not proof that all browser modules work. Inspect the iframe's module requests and JavaScript console. The API iframe fix in PR #88 externalizes the inline module; its regression checks cover the cache-busted HTML path that previously failed with HTTP 500.

A scoped WebSocket test can be run with operator permission:

kubectl -n ragnarok exec -i deployment/wsproxy -- node - < scripts/check-wsproxy.cjs

It checks a real handshake, not a game login. A new browser session should verify iframe readiness, public HOST/ports, RemoteClient/CORS and actual login/map loading. The operator confirmed login on the completed installation; continuing graphics, Lua, GRF-content or client issues are separate investigations.

docs.title: RemoteClient quick-health caveat
docs.text: The pinned RemoteClient defaults to lazy GRF indexes. Its quick health endpoint can report 503/grfsLoaded=0 before indexes are loaded, even when the mount is readable and an explicit parser/resource request succeeds. Distinguish this known metric limitation from missing DATA.INI, wrong file case, absent GRFs, permissions, real parse failures or HTTP rewrite errors. Do not enable a large index/cache solely to turn the quick metric green.

docs.title: Normal changes
docs.text:
Use approved release/image-pin PRs. Changing a local .env does not update GitOps-managed ConfigMaps. Review the non-secret rendered Git changes; existing pods need a controlled replacement to consume changed environment values. Credentials remain private; a password change may require coordinated DB/operator/game-account updates, not merely a file edit.

k8s-all.sh --check is deliberately not the active-cluster health command: it requires paused Flux for a manual-bootstrap preflight. Neither --apply nor --reconcile is the ordinary update path.

docs.title: Rollback and failure handling
docs.text:
On failure, collect scoped status/events/logs and identify the failed layer before retrying. Do not rerun installers blindly, bootstrap Flux again, format storage, reset namespaces or delete PVC/PV/Longhorn volumes.

For an image regression, inspect Git history for the last verified component pin and propose a narrow revert. Keep the other component pins unchanged, rerun required checks, then adopt through normal approved GitOps reconciliation. Tag names identify infrastructure source commits, not chronological ordering; verify the registry digest and architecture. Stable is mutable and is not a rollback record.

Emergency imperative example (requires explicit target-only approval and Flux coordination; not executed during cleanup):

kubectl -n ragnarok get deployment robrowser -o jsonpath='{range .spec.template.spec.containers[*]}{.name}{" "}{.image}{"\n"}{end}'
# Record OLD_IMAGE and the actual CONTAINER before changing anything.
kubectl -n ragnarok set image deployment/robrowser "$CONTAINER=$OLD_IMAGE"
kubectl -n ragnarok rollout status deployment/robrowser --timeout=180s

An active reconciler restores its Git desired state; make the approved rollback consistent with Git rather than leaving uncontrolled drift. Do not touch MariaDB, other deployments, configuration or storage for a frontend-only incident.

Storage/DB recovery is a separate operation with a verified backup, scope, credentials and maintenance approval. The fresh-install runbook's automatic empty-DB import is not a restore procedure.

docs.title: Image release controls
docs.text:
Main CI gates the existing Container Security workflow. It builds changed remote, robrowser, rAthena and wsProxy candidates for AMD64/ARM64, scans each platform and generates SPDX SBOMs. Publication does not rebuild them: it promotes the exact approved digest, verifies its source SHA/candidate digest and refuses a stale release when main moved during the scan.

The configured Trivy threshold is HIGH/CRITICAL, ignore-unfixed=true, exit-code=1. Fixable findings at that threshold block publishing; lower severities and unfixed findings are not equivalent blocking guarantees. A green result is not proof that every vulnerability is absent. Unchanged images are not rebuilt or rescanned just because a documentation/manifest commit reached main.

Rebuilt components provide sbom-remote, sbom-robrowser, sbom-rathena or sbom-wsproxy artifacts, each containing platform inventories. The ready-component record ties source and digest to promotion. Review the run/artifacts and registry metadata, not just stable. See image provenance.

docs.title: Runtime controls
docs.text:
The project application Deployments retain non-root UID/GID 1000, dropped Linux capabilities, no privilege escalation, runtime-default seccomp and configured probes/resources. MariaDB and infrastructure operators use their own charts/images; do not claim every cluster container uses the application UID. wsProxy also has a readonly root filesystem; frontend/PHP use separate writable runtime paths.

The namespace labels enforce Pod Security baseline and audit/warn restricted. The DB NetworkPolicy allows only the selected game/loader peers and the labeled MariaDB controller in its own namespace on TCP3306. The operator needs SQL access to reconcile Database/User/Grant; do not remove the policy or broadly open ingress as a bootstrap workaround. Client mounts remain readonly to remote.

docs.title: PHP branch and request-time hardening
docs.text:
images/remote/Dockerfile requires php84 >=8.4.27 and a build-time/runtime guard rejects PHP >=8.5 or older 8.4 packages. On Alpine 3.24 the generic CLI explicitly links to php84; Apache uses its PHP8.4 module. security.ini disables session upload progress before request parsing. TRACE/Git-path blocking and the pinned RemoteClient .htaccess remain tested. The frontend image has no Apache/PHP, and remote does not fetch the frontend tree or Node/npm.

The no-cache remote candidate build reruns Alpine package installation; apk's --no-cache alone is not Docker layer-cache invalidation. There is no scheduled PHP-package rebuild or general CI workflow_dispatch release path. New packages do not update an existing container automatically; an approved source/build change must pass the normal release/image-pin chain.

A scoped read-only diagnostic after an approved rollout can check:

kubectl -n ragnarok exec deployment/remote -- php -v
kubectl -n ragnarok exec deployment/remote -- php -r 'echo get_cfg_var("session.upload_progress.enabled"), PHP_EOL;'

Expect PHP in the permitted 8.4 branch and upload progress 0. Do not weaken checks or restart an old image and call it a security update.

docs.title: Secrets and local files
docs.text:
.env, client files and unversioned overrides are local configuration, not CI inputs automatically copied to GHCR. Keep actual credentials outside Git. The bootstrap uses the supplied .env values exactly; it does not silently generate or rotate passwords. Review template defaults before production use.

The private offline bootstrap renderer requires the operator-owned configuration, writes owner-only output and refuses overwrites. Database and interserver credentials are Secret fields; ConfigMaps contain non-secret settings only. Default --check and fake-API tests perform no installation. --apply is a separately approved cluster-changing operation and never deletes namespaces/resumes Flux.

Use SSH/credential helpers for Git authentication rather than embedding tokens in remote URLs. Do not print .git/config, git remote -v, kubeconfigs, Secret values, full environments or private bootstrap JSON in public logs. Even a URL inspection can expose a token. Redact browser/HMR token queries from diagnostics. If a credential appears in output, revoke/replace it; deleting a local log does not revoke it or remove every copy.

The upstream updater's UPSTREAM_PR_TOKEN belongs in Actions Secrets, with the minimum repository-scoped Contents/Pull requests permissions required. GitHub secret scanning, push protection and branch rules are external repository settings; verify them separately rather than assuming this Markdown enforces them. Their presence does not make leaked credentials safe or rotate them.

docs.title: Updates and recovery
docs.text:
Dependencies/base images/actions are pinned as described in upstream updates. Source/dependency auto-merge policy is separate from the draft GitOps image release approval. Active Flux adopts merged manifests automatically; it must be coordinated during emergency imperative work.

Do not use setup scripts, namespace resets, blanket image/containerd pruning or PVC/Longhorn deletion to fix an application incident. Keep private rollback and backup material, but never commit it. Follow operations and separately reviewed DB/storage recovery procedures.

docs.title: Upstream source updates and release automation
docs.text: build/dependencies.env pins the roBrowserLegacy, RemoteClient-PHP, rAthena and ROEnglishRE forks. A fork sync does not itself change a deployed image. Check Fork Updates runs every six hours (and supports workflow_dispatch), compares the configured repository HEADs, updates changed pins and validates the candidate source layouts.

docs.title: Distinct approval boundaries
docs.text:
• The source updater uses UPSTREAM_PR_TOKEN to create/update automation/upstream-dependency-update and explicitly requests squash auto-merge after required checks. Its branch-update implementation currently force-pushes that dedicated automation branch; operators should review that policy separately.
  • Dependabot checks actions, image bases and the project npm overlays. The Dependabot Auto-Merge workflow enables auto-merge only for non-draft Dependabot PRs targeting main. Required repository checks/protections still apply.
  • These are source/dependency PR behaviors. Publish opens a separate draft GitOps image-pin PR, and does not request its auto-merge. It requires release approval before an active Flux reconciler adopts it.

One source-PR body text currently says no automatic merge, but the executable workflow ends in gh pr merge --auto; this guide describes that actual behavior. This documentation cleanup does not change automation policy or enable merges.

The updater requires a repository-scoped UPSTREAM_PR_TOKEN with Contents and Pull requests write access. Keep it in Actions Secrets, never Git or chat. A workflow rerun retains its original source SHA; do not replay an old publishing run to release newer main or bypass the publication freshness/security gates.

docs.title: Validation and publication
docs.text:
CI validates the pinned Dockerfile-required source layout, API override parity, Compose/templates, translations, runtime isolation and frontend modules. Changed main candidates pass both platform scans and SBOM generation before exact-digest promotion. The workflow refuses a stale publication when main moved during scans. Unchanged image components retain their existing release tags.

roBrowserLegacy changes affect the frontend robrowser image. RemoteClient and ROEnglishRE changes affect remote. rAthena and wsProxy are separate images. The project-owned frontend package/lockfile supplies dependencies required by the pinned source, including granny-ro-js; update it deliberately when necessary. The API HTML/module override must be reviewed if upstream initialization changes.

Only after approving/merging the generated image-pin PR does active Flux adopt the changed release. See GitOps lifecycle and image provenance. Layout/module/CI checks do not prove all gameplay/content compatibility. The completed installation's successful login does not close unrelated graphics, Lua or GRF-content issues.

docs.title: Confirmed operating baseline
docs.text:
The operator confirmed on 2026-11-02:

  • K3s on Raspberry Pi and Longhorn working.
  • flux-system and ragnarok-stack active/Ready; last confirmed application revision 109430d1 after merged PRs #87, #88, #89 and #90.
  • MariaDB, rAthena login/char/map, remote, robrowser and wsProxy working: seven pods Running, each 1/1 at the one-replica baseline.
  • Ragnarok login in the real browser successful.

This is an operator-confirmed, dated observation; it was not rechecked during this documentation cleanup. Documentation-only merges may advance Flux source/applied revisions without changing application specifications. No infrastructure setup, Kubernetes deployment, Flux action or storage operation was performed during that cleanup.

docs.title: Actually executed checks from the implementation work
docs.text: Check What it established Limit Native web builds and filesystem/history boundary checks Only robrowser contains the frontend; remote contains PHP/client resources Local builds are not registry release provenance Translation SHA-256 comparisons Renewal 625 files; Pre-Renewal 684, with ten differing overlay replacements; pinned .htaccess preserved Optional translation Addons are not installed Isolated web Compose HTTP/module transformation, PHP security, routing, readonly GRF mapping, loose files and CORS Not full game login Independent override fixtures Each image serves its own marker/index after startup Ignored local overrides are not present in clean CI builds API regression on cold Vite Old cache-busted HTML proxy fails with 500; external bootstrap resolves Node protocol tests stub engine execution Registry release evidence Both architectures, source annotations, approved digest records, platform SBOMs and promotion Does not prove every client asset is correct Empty MariaDB 11.8.6 + published rAthena in isolated Docker Schema, Renewal tables and interserver account initialized automatically Not a backup/restore test Offline bootstrap fixtures and fake kubectl protocol Private rendering, credential mappings, no leaks/overwrite, aborts and ordering Not actual Kubernetes scheduling or volume provisioning Actual bootstrap --check before installation Read-only source/operator/port/bootstrap readiness on the paused target Not appropriate for normal active Flux Operator's final Kubernetes/browser test Healthy application stack and successful login Remaining rendering/Lua/content issues are not resolved

docs.title: Repeatable tests
docs.text:
See development for the local/CI commands and operations for live read-only checks. The existing PR validate gate is scope-sensitive: documentation-only changes can pass without image builds. A strict MkDocs build and local link checks are the relevant documentation validation.

The final documentation cleanup runs offline bootstrap fixture/protocol tests, syntax/Kustomize checks and a strict documentation build. It does not claim those commands execute a new real cluster installation. Future installation examples must be reviewed against the target context and current external scripts.

docs.title: Scope intentionally left open
docs.text: Graphics, Lua, GRF-content and other client/gameplay errors are separate tasks. Do not hide them by weakening security/readiness checks or resetting a working namespace/database. Capture sanitized browser/server diagnostics and use a separately reviewed fix when that work is authorized.
